messages.subject: Population names - how to completely change
messages.subject_clean: Population names - how to completely change
messages.body_plain:
Hi dartR community,

This is a rookie question that I thought I could easily solve, but haven’t been able to. I hope somebody has a quick fix.

I am working with a genlight file, and for historical reasons my pop slot is filled with labels for high-level geographic regions, whereas what I would like to have in that slot is finer scale sampling sites.  Typically there may be several sites within the regions.

The gl.recode.pop function doesn’t seem appropriate because it designed for one for one population name changes, or combining pops.

If I import a text file vector of pop names (i.e. the vector is as long as the number of individuals) and try to place it in the pop slot by e.g.

Site_names <- read.table(file = "Site_names.txt", header = FALSE)

my.gl <http://my.gl>$pop <- Site_names

I get an error like:

Error in checkSlotAssignment(object, name, value) :

  assignment of an object of class “data.frame” is not valid for slot ‘pop’ in an object of class “genlight”; is(value, "factorOrNULL") is not TRUE

I don’t have that problem if I import data into $other slots.

No doubt a basic error, but I am hoping an R guru can set me straight.

Cheers,

Olly

The solution is to have your new finer scale sampling sites as a variable in your individual metrics (added when you read the data in), then use gl.reassign.pop() to assign that metric to the pop slot.

messages.body_plain:
Thanks Arthur.

With some minor tweaking it worked!

Cheers,

Olly

--

For the record….

#Switching the "pop" name to Region - which is more appropriate

test.gl <http://test.gl>$other$Region <-test.gl <http://test.gl>$pop

#Now bring in the actual site names to the pop slot#

Site_names <- read.csv(file = "Site_names.csv", header = TRUE) #import the vector

test.gl@other$ind.metrics <- Site_names #The variable is labelled Site in the input file (header), this will be the label for the vector within ind.metrics

test.gl <http://test.gl> <- gl.reassign.pop(test.gl <http://test.gl>,as.pop="Site") #The function looks in ind.metrics for a vector called Site

test.gl <http://test.gl> #have a look

levels(test.gl <http://test.gl>$pop)

levels(test.gl <http://test.gl>$other$Region)

messages.subject: Converting DArT data to COANCESTORY format
messages.subject_clean: Converting DArT data to COANCESTORY format
messages.body_plain:
Hey guys,

Does anyone know of a script that can convert DArT data into the format that COANCESTORY takes?

I am particularly keen on obtaining Wang's relatedness estimators for my dataset.

Any help would be greatly appreciated, thanks in advanced!

Kind regards,
Chad

Any help

messages.subject: RE: [dartR] Converting DArT data to COANCESTORY format
messages.subject_clean: [dartR] Converting DArT data to COANCESTORY format
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I was just toying again with ways to get relatedness into dartR (as quite some people are requesting it).

Here is an approach that did not work some time ago as the package relatedness seemed not to work reliably with a greater number of SNPs. Seems to be better now. So in case someone wants to test this here is the way to do it:

Install package related “by hand”.
Replace the line x<- bandicoot.gl <http://bandicoot.gl>  with x <- yourgenlight object
Run the rest of the script and modify the coancestry part, if you want to have different estimates

In case you want to export to run the gui, you should be able to uncomment the write.table command below. [I have not tested it to run with coancestry yet].

In case it works please let me know, then I will add a function to dartR.

Relatedness is a package that wraps around the fortran code of coancestry so should have identical results. If some can check that would be great.

Cheers, Bernd

#install.packages("related", repos="http://R-Forge.R-project.org")

library(related)

x <- bandicoot.gl <http://bandicoot.gl>[1:10,]#[1:10,1:7]

gd <- as.matrix(x)

mm <- matrix(NA, nrow=nrow(gd), ncol =ncol(gd)*2 )

mm[, seq(1,nLoc(x)*2,2)] <- gd

mm <- ifelse(mm==1,0,mm)

mm[, seq(2,nLoc(x)*2,2)] <- gd

mm <- ifelse(mm==1,2,mm)

mm <- mm+1

mm <- ifelse(is.na <http://is.na>(mm),0,mm)

gtd <- data.frame(V1=as.character(indNames(x)), mm)

gtd$V1 <- as.character(gtd$V1)

#export as file

#write.table(gtd, file = "gtd.txt", sep = "\t",col.names = F, row.names = F)

#load from file

#gtd <- readgenotypedata("gtd.txt")$gdata

#---Calculate Relatedness---#

output <- coancestry(gtd, lynchrd=2, quellergt=2, wang=2)

#---View Point Estimates---#

output$relatedness
